title: Quiz — Security Controls and Protection Techniques

questions.q: Which control detects without blocking and is placed out-of-path from traffic?
questions.explain: A NIDS is detective: it receives a copy of traffic via SPAN/tap and does not interrupt the flow.

questions.q: Which mechanism verifies that an email was signed by the sending domain?
questions.explain: DKIM adds a cryptographic signature verifiable via the public key published in DNS. SPF lists authorized sending servers.

questions.q: Which technologies fall under deception? (Select all that apply)
questions.explain: Honeynets, honeytokens, and canary accounts are decoys. A HIDS is a host-based detection agent.

questions.q: Match each control to the layer it protects.
questions.explain: Choosing the right control means identifying the layer and traffic flow affected by the risk.

questions.q: An attacker compromises a workstation and attempts to modify system files. Which host control can block the action?
questions.explain: A HIPS is a preventive host agent: it blocks suspicious behavior locally. A HIDS would only alert.

questions.q: Which statement about EDR is correct?
options: It is an agent installed on the endpoint to detect and respond
It is an email DNS record
It is a centralized logging server
questions.explain: EDR is an endpoint agent. Calling it a 'next generation firewall' is a known error in SOC Notes that is corrected here.
